name: Cohorts, Funnels & Window Functions
goal: The senior-analyst sprint — trend, rank within groups, build a retention cohort, and compute a funnel from the dirty clickstream you must clean first.

brief.body: This is the stuff investors get excited about. Three things for the growth story: month-over-month revenue with growth rates, a retention cohort showing whether customers stick around, and our purchase funnel from the web logs — how many sessions go view → cart → checkout → buy. Heads up: the web events table is raw and ugly. Engineering hasn't cleaned it. That's part of the job.

clinic.title: Window functions in anger
clinic.body: LAG() reaches to the previous period (growth %); SUM() OVER (ORDER BY …) gives running totals; ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY m) ranks within groups; FIRST_VALUE() anchors a cohort's starting size for retention %. Master PARTITION BY … ORDER BY … and most analytics opens up.

classwork.title: Monthly cohort retention — together (DuckDB date functions)

steps.checkpoint: A sensible new-customers-per-month series — each cohort's month-0 size. Spark: DATE_FORMAT(first_dt,'yyyy-MM').

steps.instr: Compute the month offset of every order (count DISTINCT customers).
steps.sql:
WITH first_order AS (
  SELECT CustomerID, MIN(OrderDate) AS first_dt FROM orders GROUP BY CustomerID),
activity AS (
  SELECT strftime(f.first_dt,'%Y-%m') AS cohort_month,
    date_diff('month', date_trunc('month', f.first_dt), date_trunc('month', o.OrderDate)) AS month_offset,
    o.CustomerID
  FROM orders o JOIN first_order f ON o.CustomerID = f.CustomerID)
SELECT cohort_month, month_offset, COUNT(DISTINCT CustomerID) AS active
FROM activity GROUP BY cohort_month, month_offset
ORDER BY cohort_month, month_offset;
steps.checkpoint: month_offset = 0 equals the cohort size from step 1. DISTINCT customers — counting order rows would double-count repeat buyers. Spark: MONTHS_BETWEEN(...).

classwork.reference:
WITH first_order AS (
  SELECT CustomerID, MIN(OrderDate) AS first_dt FROM orders GROUP BY CustomerID),
activity AS (
  SELECT strftime(f.first_dt,'%Y-%m') AS cohort_month,
    date_diff('month', date_trunc('month', f.first_dt), date_trunc('month', o.OrderDate)) AS month_offset,
    o.CustomerID
  FROM orders o JOIN first_order f ON o.CustomerID = f.CustomerID),
sized AS (
  SELECT cohort_month, month_offset, COUNT(DISTINCT CustomerID) AS active
  FROM activity GROUP BY cohort_month, month_offset)
SELECT cohort_month, month_offset, active,
  ROUND(active * 100.0 / FIRST_VALUE(active) OVER (PARTITION BY cohort_month ORDER BY month_offset), 1) AS retention_pct
FROM sized ORDER BY cohort_month, month_offset;

tickets.title: MoM net revenue, growth %, and running total
tickets.prompt: Monthly net revenue 2022-2024 with MoM growth % and a cumulative running total. Output exactly five columns in order: month (use the OrderMonth column, which is already 'YYYY-MM'), net_revenue (rounded 0), prev_month (rounded 0), mom_growth_pct (rounded 1), running_total (rounded 0). One row per calendar month, chronological. The first month's prev_month and mom_growth_pct are NULL.
acceptanceCriteria: One row per month, chronological (36 rows)
MoM growth % via LAG, divide-by-zero guarded with NULLIF
Cumulative running total via windowed SUM
hints: LAG(net_rev) OVER (ORDER BY OrderMonth) for prev_month.
SUM(net_rev) OVER (ORDER BY OrderMonth) for running_total.

tickets.title: Clean the clickstream & compute the purchase funnel
tickets.prompt: The full real-world gauntlet, from raw raw_web_events. Dedup re-delivered events (by event_id), normalise event_type casing/whitespace, then compute the session funnel. Output exactly eight columns in order: viewed, carted, checkout, purchased, view_to_cart_pct, cart_to_checkout_pct, checkout_to_purchase_pct, overall_conversion_pct — all percentages rounded to 1 decimal, divide-by-zero guarded. Stages map to event_type: page_view, add_to_cart, checkout_start, purchase.
acceptanceCriteria: Duplicate event_id rows removed (ROW_NUMBER per event_id = 1)
event_type normalised (LOWER+TRIM) so casing variants collapse
Funnel uses COUNT(DISTINCT session_id) per stage
Conversion % per step + overall, guarded with NULLIF
hints: deduped CTE: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY event_id ORDER BY event_ts), keep rn=1.
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN et='page_view' THEN session_id END) for each stage.
tickets.selfCheck: The grader checks the funnel row. The full portfolio version also parses the mixed timestamp formats and counts the unparseable rows (don't hide them) — do that as a second query for your write-up. DuckDB: try_strptime(event_ts,'%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'); Spark: try_to_timestamp(...).
